0.text: I wish I were anywhere else. I wish I were SOMEONE else.

1.text: I can't believe it: my second time setting out and I didn't find a single ray of sunlight.

2.text: There's no sign of any tunnel I might've fallen through to get here, caved-in or otherwise.

3.text: If I could find it and see some daylight, it would give me an idea of how long I've been down here for.

4.text: My phone still won't turn on, and the ceiling's just a craggy mess that I can't make out most of the time.

5.text: On top of that, the food in my backpack really hasn't stretched far.

6.text: If I see Joe again, I'm going to scream at him about how awful this trip has turned out to be.

7.text: Sure, total solar eclipses are rare, but seeing one wasn't worth this catastrophe.

8.text: When Nick and I agreed to this, I really liked the idea of traveling out west and camping with our friends for a few nights.

9.text: Now, at this stage, I don't know if I'll see any of them again.

10.text: I'll probably need to try drinking the water in these pools around me soon, although that faint glow has me worried.

11.text: I can add that to the list of things I can't really explain.

12.text: Even if I can't drink from them, the pools ARE illuminating the cavern a surprising amount.

13.text: Though, I'm afraid to wander too close to the long, jagged shadows they're casting.

0.text: Those other shadows were contorted. Writhing. Like thousands of hands reaching out towards us.

1.text: They felt so cold as they closed in on our feet.

2.text: In retrospect, I really don't know where we were trying to run to.

3.text: We were surrounded by trees and the trail would have only taken us deeper into the woods.

5.text: I'm completely useless on my own.

6.text: I don't think I'm going to find my way out.

7.text: Even if anyone else ended up down here, all I've heard are dull echoes in the distance.

0.text: Maybe my next time setting out will be better.

1.text: Even if it isn't, no one will find me if I keep hiding out in this nook.

2.text: Yes, it's time to get going, Mary.

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: Umm . . . maybe . . . if it's going to get me no matter what . . .

5.text: Me neither, although whatever that thing was, it was difficult to make out.

6.speaker: Nick
6.text: Never mind any of that, though: how hurt are you?

7.speaker: Mary
7.text: Hngh, I already wasn't doing great, but now I'm really not.

8.speaker: Nick
8.text: Well, here, it seems safe for now.

9.speaker: Nick
9.text: Let's take a moment to recover a bit.

10.speaker: Nick
10.text: I have some medicine, bandages, extra water, and a few other goodies I packed for our hike . . .

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: How long was that thing after you for?

1.speaker: Nick
1.text: Not very long, although I'm not sure how long it was watching me for.

2.speaker: Nick
2.text: Not to sound too out there, but when it first approached me, it looked like it was crawling out of the shadows.

3.speaker: Nick
3.text: I tried defending myself, but I didn't really have anything that I could hurt it with.

4.speaker: Mary
4.text: Hey, speaking of "out there," did it also use . . . psychic powers against you?

6.speaker: Nick
6.text: My head began hurting when it approached, kind of like a brain freeze or something.

8.speaker: Nick
8.text: Yeah, I'm having a hard time understanding anything that's been going on here.

0.text: I'm really happy that I found you, Nick.

2.speaker: Nick
